title.value: 30×30 biodiversity gains rely on national coordination
title.justification: The paper explores the implementation and effectiveness of the 30x30 biodiversity goal, emphasizing national coordination.
title.quote: Global commitments to protect 30% of land by 2030 present an opportunity to combat the biodiversity crisis, but reducing extinction risk will depend on where countries expand protection.

extractions.description: This paper investigates the potential biodiversity gains that can result from coordinated national efforts to protect 30% of land by 2030. It uses Canada as a model to assess different conservation scenarios that prioritize biodiversity facets and coordinate protection strategies to maximize biodiversity capture in protected areas while considering climate change impacts.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is about biodiversity conservation under the framework of protecting 30% of land by 2030, which directly relates to sustainability efforts in ecological systems.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Protected areas are pivotal to biodiversity conservation, but existing networks are inadequate when it comes to safeguarding Earth’s biodiversity under climate change.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on strategies for the protection and preservation of biodiversity, making 'Natural Systems Protection' the most relevant category.
primary_category.quote: Global commitments to protect 30% of land by 2030 present an opportunity to combat the biodiversity crisis, but reducing extinction risk will depend on where countries expand protection.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper addresses the need to incorporate climate change into spatial planning for conservation, highlighting the importance of climate adaptations strategies.
secondary_categories.quote: Our results show that nationally coordinated strategies can enable large conservation gains and efficiently serve global goals, while also benefiting regional conservation projects by providing broader context for local decisions.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category of 'Biodiversity' aligns with the paper's focus on conserving a wide range of species and biodiversity facets within the 30x30 framework.
primary_sub_category.quote: Here, we explore how different approaches to reaching 30x30 incur trade-offs and impact our ability to protect a broad range of biodiversity.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper discusses national strategies as a means to prevent biodiversity crisis, similar to relief efforts in approach.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our results confirm the importance of having biodiversity-informed national strategies for 30 × 30. Spatial planning that incorporates climate change, overcomes bias in biodiversity data, and accounts for uncertainty is both feasible and necessary.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The incorporation of climate change and its impacts on conservation areas is akin to climate risk modeling.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: National strategies for 30 × 30 can also facilitate spatial planning for climate resilience. Increasingly, evidence suggests that biodiversity in protected areas, despite being safeguarded from land use change, is still threatened by climate change.

applications.justification: The paper suggests the use of biodiversity indicators to aid in spatial planning for conservation efforts.
applications.quote: Biodiversity indicators can be mapped for thousands of species and functional and phylogenetic facets link taxa to functioning ecosystems, future option values, and millions of years of evolutionary history.

applications.justification: Strategies for identifying climate refugia are part of the paper's approach to conservation planning under changing climates.
applications.quote: To incorporate climate change, we down-weighted future projections to account for uncertainty and to prioritize "win-win" areas of overlap between current and future ranges.

applications.justification: The central recommendation of the paper is the development of nationally coordinated strategies for achieving biodiversity conservation goals by 2030.
applications.quote: These findings confirm the critical need for national strategies for reaching 30×30 and demonstrate the importance of quantifying indicators and assessing trade-offs to facilitate biodiversity-informed conservation planning.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper fits well within the existing category of 'Natural Systems Protection' with a focus on 'Biodiversity.'
new_primary_category.quote: Global commitments to protect 30% of land by 2030 present an opportunity to combat the biodiversity crisis, but reducing extinction risk will depend on where countries expand protection.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: It fits into existing sub-categories of 'Biodiversity'.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Using Canada as a model nation, we evaluate how well each scenario captures biodiversity using scalable indicators while accounting for climate change, data bias, and uncertainty.
